reviews.title: Great case
reviews.comment: Plenty of space to build in. Plenty of cooling for fans and aio. Also storage. With corsair ssd adapter I was able to fit in 8 ssds. Used lian li edge psu. Made it that much easier for cable routing. It is a great value for what you get as well as quality of build. The all black build with this case imo looks fantastic, see pic.
reviews.author: Robert Grover

reviews.title: Massive case!  Make sure you have space for it!
reviews.comment:
The media could not be loaded.  https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/C1dxvccHPfL.mp4 https://m.media-amazon.com/images/I/61zJ4Bl5fbL._SY256.jpg I’ve done many cases over the years.  Thermaltake.  Antec.  Lian-Li.  NZXT.  Coolermaster.  I’ve always found myself going back to Antec, as they have excellent layouts and everything you’d want in a case.  This C8 is no exception.  Lots of fan options, 98% tool-less, little niceties like an included small bin to organize your extra screws.  Front panel connector is now a single line instead of all those little connectors you have to read schematics to put in because you can’t remember Intel’s layout when you build a new PC once every few years.  Purchased Antec Non-A RBG fans to go with it, since this doesn’t include any.  Not a big deal.  Lots if space on the backside for SSDs and 3.5” drives if you are still rockin’ those.  Panels come off easily and are secured just as fast, and you can rest assured they aren’t going to jiggle around.  Motherboard installed easily, lots of airflow and barely audible even with 10 120mm fans.  Even pushing it hard during a stress test the fans never spun past 600 RPM.  68F ambient temperature.  CPU and Asus AIO keeps the Intel i5-12600k around 32-37c, even under heavy gaming with Starfield at max settings.  The video card fans barely even spin up due to the cooling from the bottom intakes.  Excellent quality case.  Front side and bottom are intakes, rear single 120mm for exhaust, and plenty of room for my 360mm AIO and 3 120mm exhaust fans up top.
If you have the space, this is what you want.  Again, its MASSIVE.  Not Thermaltake Tower 500 massive but still huge in its own right.  See video for fan audible levels during idle.
reviews.author: Derick C.

reviews.title: very nice case at a great price
reviews.comment: Love this case. plenty of room for everything inside and it looks great. the cooling setup options are good as well. I have my AIO rad mounted in the top as an exhaust, 3 x140mm fans in the bottom as intake to blow straight up into the GPU, 1 x140mm in the back as exhaust, and 3 x120mm in the front side as intake. temps stay nice and cool. I love that it is a toolless design and there are plenty of tie points and bundle straps for cable management. it IS very wide compared to standard ATX cases but that is because of its dual chamber design that helps with cooling.
reviews.author: brenton ward

reviews.title: Crosair? NZXT? No thanks, I'll take this at half the price & better design!!!
reviews.comment:
I don't write reviews often but I must because this is such a great case!! It's been serving me so well for 8 months now!
I was looking for more intake and better ventilation for my 360mm 38mm rad and I found it here! With the original case the NZXT H710i I was getting high CPU temps, upwards of 82-83°, mostly due to constriction on my rad, despite 40mm being the limit for size on the H710i but we all know now NZXT is mostly garbage. Instructions were clear, came with everything I needed to move my parts over, ample space for the fan controller, GREAT and I mean GREAT cable management avenues, bottom & side intakes is superior than front, fits my RTX 4080 Super nicely, and the case itself looks and feels great!
Specs
CPU: AMD 5950x
GPU: MSI 4080 Super Suprim X
RAM: 48GB on 4 sticks
PSU: MSI 1000W 80 Platinum
Fans: 3x 140mm bottom intake
3x 120mm side intake
1x 140mm rear exhaust
3x 120mm 3000RPM + high pressure top exhaust (38mm 360 rad)
reviews.author: Amazon Customer

reviews.title: My cat and my PS5 are now roommates.
reviews.comment:
So here I was.... I was in the market for a new E-ATX case because I needed a little more room for cable management. When the Antec C8 arrived, I think the delivery driver needed to take a break. I thought there was a mistake and they'd shipped me a server rack or perhaps a small refrigerator. That might have been one of the biggest boxes that has set its graces upon my eyes!
Building in this thing is less of a challenge and more of an echo-location exercise! Every time I open the front panel I feel like I'm Cave Diving! I dropped one of the AIO cooler screws and I’m pretty sure I heard it land three seconds later! Kid you not!  The airflow is phenomenal, mostly because the case has developed its own weather system!
But the real story is the sheer, unadulterated space! After installing my brand new Asrock X870e Taichi Lite motherboard, a comically large GPU (The Gigabyte 9060XT), the power supply, all 6 sata drives, and seven fans, it looked... empty. Lonely, even. And also the dust filter on the bottom! Absolutely perfect! I can't forget it because I have so many pets! Its perfect to block fur from getting into your build!
So Anyways, I did what any logical person would do! I put my PS5 Inside! Plenty of room!
And while I was doing such ridiculous demented things, My cat hopped in and he just stared at me! Like it was HIS HOME!
I am not joking. My entire PC, a PlayStation 5, and a 12-pound cat are currently living inside the new case! . There is still enough room to start a small herb garden! My cat and my PS5 now split the rent, which is great for my budget! Perfect Case Overall!
reviews.author: Ben Williams
